transcript:
Meeting: NovusGrid x Redwood - Streaming & p95 throughput discovery
Date/Time: 2028-07-21 16:30 UTC
Duration: 57 minutes
Attendees: Ethan Morales (Redwood AE), Priya Singh (Redwood SE), Liam O'Connor (NovusGrid CTO), Maya Chen (NovusGrid SRE Lead), Diego Ramos (NovusGrid Platform Eng)

Summary:
NovusGrid is evaluating Redwood Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private for low-latency streaming use cases (live telemetry summarization and conversational agent overlays in their control UI). Primary goals are p95 latency targets for streaming token delivery, steady-state token/sec throughput, and cost predictability under bursty daytime loads. They have strict SOC2/SSO/KMS requirements and need private networking options for some tenants. Redwood AE/SE discussed batching, KV cache, quantization, routing/fallbacks and proposed running a short POC with sample prompts and telemetry trace.

Topics:
- Current stack and pain points
- p95 targets and what counts as p95 for streaming (end-to-end vs server gen)
- Concurrency and token/sec sizing; burst buffering strategies
- Dedicated capacity tradeoffs and private VPC packaging
- Security compliance: SOC 2, SAML/SSO, KMS, audit logs
- Next steps and POC scope

Action items (captured mid-call):
- Ethan: cost/latency spreadsheet comparing Hosted vs Dedicated for their usage patterns
- Priya: streaming benchmark harness and example Redwood config (batching, kv cache hints)
- Liam: upload 3 prompt families + two weeks of telemetry showing peak windows

Transcript body:
[00:00] Ethan Morales: hey everyone, thanks for joining, i'm ethan from redwood, with priya on the call, we'll run through a quick discovery on your streaming latency and throughput needs, then talk options hosted vs dedicated vs private, and next steps for a POC.
[00:14] Liam O'Connor: yeah thanks, um quick intro, i'm liam, cto at novusgrid, we do edge telemetry aggregation for grid ops, need low latency overlays on our control dashboards, typically sub 300ms end-to-end p95 for short prompts, and streaming partial tokens matter because operators want early hints.
[00:31] Priya Singh: great, thanks liam, sub 300ms p95 is a tight target for streaming; when you say end-to-end, do you mean from operator click to first token visible in UI or from request hitting redwood to token?
[00:45] Liam: whole path, so that includes our edge hop + network to redwood + model generation until first token. we can isolate the server-side p95 requirement to ~200ms to leave room for network.
[00:58] Maya Chen: to add, our peak concurrencies are during incident windows — roughly 180-220 concurrent sessions in a region, tokens per second per session varies, but median 8-12 tps and peak bursts up to 80 tps for short 20s windows.
[01:18] Diego Ramos: right and we have occasional global bursts when multiple regions sync, that once a week lasts 3-5 minutes. we need graceful degradation and predictable cost.
[01:30] Priya: okay that's very helpful. can you confirm what models you're currently using and whether you do any local quantized inference today?
[01:40] Liam: currently we call openai for most user flows, but we've also experimented with an in-house triton stack for on-prem testing — quality is okay but ops cost is high, and streaming there is rough. so exploring redwood to avoid building infra, but we need either dedicated reserved pools or private for security-sensitive tenants.
[01:58] Ethan: makes sense. for sizing, two main knobs — concurrency (how many simultaneous sessions) and tokens/sec per session. we usually translate that to tokens/sec aggregate and then to capacity using model profile (tokens/sec per GPU) and batching assumptions. for streaming, p95 is driven by scheduling delay + model token generation time + network.
[02:18] Maya: are you able to give a rough tokens/sec per GPU number for, say, a 7B-ish or 13B-ish model? we need those ballpark figures to evaluate Dedicated cost.
[02:29] Priya: yes, ballpark: for a quantized 13B on current kernels you might see ~700-1,200 tokens/sec steady-state per GPU for non-streaming batched requests; streaming with small prefix windows and continuous KV cache may be lower per-session due to smaller effective batch sizes — but aggregate throughput can still reach similar numbers if requests batch. we can share more precise profiles in the benchmark template.
[02:58] Liam: okay and p95? like what p95 for token latency given 200 concurrent sessions?
[03:05] Priya: depends a lot on batching window — if you allow a 20-30ms batching window you get better GPU utilization but add to latency. with dedicated Reserved pools and aggressive caching (prefix caching for repeated prompts), server-side p95 for first token can be in the 120-180ms range on optimized configs. Hosted bursty scenarios might have higher p95 if they hit cold starts or shared pool contention.
[03:36] Diego: we are particularly sensitive to tail latency. how do you handle fallbacks — say one zone has capacity pressure?
[03:44] Ethan: routing policies — we can route by latency SLO to a regional pool, fall back to a lower-cost model variant, or spill to dedicated reserved capacity if available. the platform supports automatic fallback policies and circuit-breakers so you can maintain throughput at slightly different quality.
[04:04] Maya: security question — for private tenants we need VPC peering and customer-managed KMS for key wrapping, plus SAML SSO and audit logs forwarded to our SIEM. is that all supported?
[04:16] Priya: yes, for Redwood Private we offer VPC peering and optional customer KMS/HSM integrations, SAML SSO and audit log streaming. our security pack (i'll share) has SOC2 report, network diagrams, and encryption details.
[04:32] Liam: good. another question — do you have tooling to measure p95 server-only vs end-to-end? we prefer to stamp server p95 separately in our dashboards.
[04:41] Priya: we expose per-request metrics, p50/p95/p99 for generation latency, token throughput, and broken-down stages (queueing, scheduling, generation). you can push traces or pull via our tracing hooks. we also produce token-level cost and latency breakdowns in the console.
[05:00] Diego: i want to understand more about streaming specifics — prefix/kvcache and continuous decoding for long sessions, how do you handle memory for KV cache at scale?
[05:10] Priya: KV cache memory is managed per-session; we provide eviction policies and incentive for prefix caching — if you see repeated prompts we can reuse KV cache to avoid re-encoding. for very long histories we recommend summarization to keep memory bounded. quantized kernels reduce memory footprint as well.
[05:29] Liam: what's the expected overhead for enabling strong encryption and KMS? does that add latency?
[05:35] Ethan: minimal on-path latency — KMS operations are typically used for key wrapping/unwrapping at session start, not per-token, so runtime token latency is unaffected. network encryption and our optimized runtime add very small overheads versus pure compute time.
[05:50] Maya: let's talk numbers for the POC: we want a server-side p95 target of 180ms for first token, support 200 concurrent sessions with median 10 tps and peak bursts to 80 tps per session for 3-5 minutes. can Redwood simulate load and produce token/sec and p95 results using our prompt sets?
[06:10] Priya: absolutely. our benchmark harness can replay your prompt families with the same token distribution and burst patterns. we'll run both hosted and dedicated profiles so you can see tradeoffs.
[06:20] Liam: and cost — we need a predictable committed price if we go Dedicated, otherwise Hosted is easier to start. can you show both models in a spreadsheet?
[06:30] Ethan: yes, i'll produce a tailored cost model mapping tokens/sec and peak capacity to Dedicated reserved GPUs vs per-token hosted pricing. i'll also include a scenario with autoscaling and burst capacity costs.
[06:42] Diego: side question — for on-prem/on-premise private bundles, do you ship a package or do you expect us to install?
[06:50] Priya: for Private we support a customer-managed control plane and an on-prem runner package. installation varies by environment; our solutions engineering team can run an install workshop during POC.
[07:02] Maya: any limitations on streaming functions like function-calling or tooling while streaming? some vendor implementations buffer function calls and that can blow up latency.
[07:12] Priya: our streaming stack supports function/tool calling with early signal events; there are configuration knobs — you can choose to emit partial tokens while holding function outputs or fanout calls after a delimiter. we'll demo patterns during POC.
[07:27] Liam: good. what about quality regressions if we use quantized models? we care about preserving operator instruction accuracy.
[07:35] Priya: quantization can slightly affect logits and occasionally produce small quality deltas; Redwood Optimize provides recommended quantization profiles by workload and we can pin model variants. as part of POC we'll run your eval prompts and report delta metrics so you can judge acceptance criteria.
[07:52] Ethan: could you share a quick sketch of acceptable quality tradeoffs? is a 1-2% drop in some eval metric acceptable if latency drops 40%?
[08:02] Liam: depends on the metric; for safety/critical ops we can't compromise. for UI hints maybe a small drop is acceptable. we should mark critical prompt families as non-negotiable.
[08:13] Diego: timeline — we're aiming for a pilot in mid-august to correlate with a release. is that doable?
[08:20] Ethan: yes, that's feasible. proposed timeline: this week exchange prompts and telemetry, week of 8/6 kickoff POC, two-week run, final readout mid-august.
[08:30] Maya: fine. technical nit: does Redwood support region pinning per-tenant and cross-region failover without reconnecting clients?
[08:39] Priya: we support regional routing and session affinity; cross-region failover may require a short reconnect depending on network topology, but we have patterns to minimize UI disruption (state handoff and KV cache rehydration).
[08:54] Liam: about burst behavior — when you say you can spill to dedicated or lower-quality models, what's the fallback latency impact?
[09:01] Priya: fallback to a smaller model variant typically reduces generation latency per token; however, for first token you might see a small delta since model gen speed sometimes scales non-linearly. we'll include concrete numbers in the POC.
[09:14] Diego: would love an example: for a 13B quantized vs a 7B, what's p95 for first token under 200 concurrent sessions?
[09:25] Priya: rough ballpark only — on dedicated pools, first token p95 could be 120-180ms for a 13B optimized run, and 80-130ms on a 7B; again these depend on batching windows and network. we'll provide actual bench outputs.
[09:45] Ethan: operational questions — what telemetry do you want from novusgrid so the POC is useful?
[09:51] Liam: we can provide sample prompt families, token length distributions, and a 2-week trace of concurrency by minute. we can also provide a couple of synthetic peak windows.
[10:02] Priya: perfect. please include operator UI flows that emit early-stop tokens so we can measure first-token visibility.
[10:11] Maya: about metrics — we need p95 server-only, p95 end-to-end, and token/sec sustained and peak. also request-level cost attribution.
[10:20] Priya: we can provide all of that. console exposes token-level cost and latency and per-route breakdown.
[10:26] Liam: ok great. any blockers around compliance for our regulated customers?
[10:33] Ethan: none novel — Private includes the controls you'd expect. we'll share SOC2 and network diagrams. for tenant-isolation we recommend Dedicated or Private depending on how strict your data residency is.
[10:44] Diego: last technical: do you support partial retransmit for clients so if tokens are delayed we can resend ranges?
[10:50] Priya: we support idempotent request IDs and streaming sequence numbers so clients can request missing ranges — useful for flaky networks.
[11:00] Liam: that's helpful. ok let's recap and nail next steps.
[11:04] Ethan: recap: Redwood will send cost model + hosted vs dedicated comparison, Priya will share benchmark harness and security pack, NovusGrid will upload prompts and telemetry. we'll schedule POC kickoff week of 8/6.
[11:19] Maya: action items noted. one more ask — can you include an example config for batching/windowing settings you'd recommend for our profile?
[11:26] Priya: yes will include recommended batching windows and cache hints tuned for streaming operator workloads.
[11:32] Liam: perfect. thanks everyone.
[11:35] Ethan: thanks all — we'll follow up with the docs and calendar invites.

End of transcript.
